name: Tree Basics
description: A binary tree node connects to left and right children, creating a recursive structure.
exampleJava: class TreeNode { int val; TreeNode left, right; }
commonMistakes: Forgetting null child checks
Treating trees like arrays without traversal logic

name: Recursive Tree Traversal
description: Visit the current node before, between, or after recursive calls to children.
commonMistakes: Missing the base case root == null
Using the wrong visit order

name: Level Order Traversal
description: Use a queue to process the tree level by level from left to right.
commonMistakes: Trying to do true level order with plain recursion
Not snapshotting the level size before iterating a level

name: Tree Height
description: The height of a tree is 1 plus the maximum height of its children.
commonMistakes: Counting edges when the problem expects node count
Returning 1 instead of 0 for null in node-based height definitions

name: Tree Diameter
description: Track the longest path passing through each node while computing heights.
commonMistakes: Recomputing heights from scratch at every node
Confusing height with diameter

name: Tree Path Contribution
description: Return the best downward contribution from a node so its parent can combine subtree results safely.
commonMistakes: Returning both-branch sums upward instead of one downward contribution
Letting negative child paths reduce the contribution instead of clipping them

name: Balanced Tree Check
description: A tree is balanced if the left and right subtree heights differ by at most 1 at every node.
commonMistakes: Checking only the root balance
Doing O(n^2) repeated height calls

name: BST Search
description: Use BST ordering to move left or right instead of scanning the entire tree.
exampleJava: if (target < root.val) root = root.left; else root = root.right;
commonMistakes: Ignoring the ordering property and traversing both sides
Going the wrong direction for comparisons

name: BST Insert and Delete
description: Insert by descending to the correct null child, and delete by handling 0, 1, or 2 child cases.
commonMistakes: Losing a subtree when reconnecting nodes
Not replacing a two-child node correctly

name: Tree Views
description: Capture visible nodes from a direction using BFS or ordered DFS.
commonMistakes: Taking every node instead of one per level
Mixing left view with level order output

name: Tree Boundary Traversal
description: Traverse left boundary, leaves, and reversed right boundary without duplicating leaf nodes.
commonMistakes: Adding leaf nodes twice through both boundary and leaf passes
Forgetting to reverse the right boundary order at the end

name: Tree Vertical Ordering
description: Group nodes by column while preserving row/depth order and value tie-breaking inside the same position.
exampleJava: columns.computeIfAbsent(col, k -> new ArrayList<>()).add(new int[] {row, node.val});
commonMistakes: Tracking only column but not row when multiple nodes land in the same vertical
Forgetting to sort equal-position nodes by value before output

name: Search Value in Binary Tree
description: Search both subtrees recursively until the target value is found or the tree is exhausted.
exampleJava: return root.val == target || contains(root.left, target) || contains(root.right, target);
commonMistakes: Stopping after checking only one subtree
Using BST ordering logic on a general binary tree

name: Root to Node Path
description: Carry a partial path through recursion and keep it only when the target is found.
exampleJava: path.add(root.val); if (dfs(root.left, target, path)) return true;
commonMistakes: Forgetting to backtrack when a branch fails
Returning a partial path that never reaches the target

name: LCA Using Paths
description: Build both root-to-node paths and compare them until the paths diverge.
commonMistakes: Comparing nodes from the end instead of from the root
Assuming equal path lengths

name: Count Targets in Subtree
description: Return how many target values are present in a subtree so parent calls can combine match information.
exampleJava: return (root.val == p || root.val == q ? 1 : 0) + leftCount + rightCount;
commonMistakes: Not adding the current node match to child counts
Throwing away one subtree count when both sides matter

name: Lowest Common Ancestor
description: Use one postorder-style pass that returns the answer as soon as the recursion learns enough from left, right, and current node matches.
exampleJava: if (left != null && right != null) return root;
commonMistakes: Returning too early when only one side has a match
Not handling the case where root is one of the targets

name: Tree Construction
description: Rebuild the tree by using traversal order properties and subtree boundaries.
commonMistakes: Not splitting the inorder range correctly
Using linear search repeatedly instead of an index map

name: Serialize Tree
description: Encode tree structure explicitly so null children and branching are preserved.
commonMistakes: Omitting null markers
Producing an encoding that cannot be decoded uniquely

name: Root-to-Leaf Path Strings
description: Build every root-to-leaf path while carrying the current path text or path state through recursion.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to emit a path only when a leaf is reached
Mutating one shared path incorrectly across sibling branches
